walkthroughs.body_html:
Diseases & Immunity — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Diseases & Immunity brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Diseases & Immunity.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A secondary immune response is faster because of:
options: More antigens
Memory cells
Fewer pathogens
Increased phagocytes

mcqs.q: How do vaccines protect you from a disease?
options: Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
Vaccines kill the pathogen if it ever enters the body.
They expose your immune system to a harmless form of the pathogen so memory cells form, allowing rapid response if exposed later.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9?
options: Guide RNA is the new sequence that gets inserted into the genome.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
It directs Cas9 to the specific DNA sequence to cut by base-pairing with the target.
Plants only photosynthesise and do not respire; respiration is for animals only.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
Yes — plants respire all the time to release energy; they also photosynthesise when there is light.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
